Tried reading the owner_index==-1 store as `(u8)(s32)&Value_00000000` (matching the pool-loaded-zero idiom the sibling owner 080a602c and this owner's own literal pool both carry at the same relative position -- both .s files embed the identical `.4byte 0x00000000 / .4byte 0x03001f2c` pair right after that branch) instead of a plain `= 0`. This reads as a register-pressure/scheduling gap on an otherwise-correct control-flow reconstruction, not a missing behavior -- a future pass should try re-deriving which local variable the compiler prioritizes into which callee-saved register (e.g. dropping the separate 'offset' local and inlining `party_slot+28` at both use sites, mirroring how the reference recomputes r2 fresh rather than keeping a single named local alive) together with the Value_00000000 spelling.
